name: JavaScript
description: The language itself: types, scope, hoisting, closures, this, prototypes and the event loop — no frameworks.

sections.title: Basics & Data Types
sections.description: What kind of language JavaScript is, its primitive and reference types, and the quirks interviewers love.

questions.question: What are the primitive types in JavaScript, and how do they differ from objects?
What is the difference between `null` and `undefined`?
Is JavaScript pass-by-value or pass-by-reference? How do you compare two objects?
What kind of language is JavaScript? (single-threaded, dynamically typed, JIT-compiled)
What does `typeof` return, and what are its quirks?
What is `NaN`, and what is the difference between `isNaN()` and `Number.isNaN()`?
What are truthy and falsy values in JavaScript?
What are template literals, and what can they do that normal strings cannot?
What is the difference between `slice`, `substring` and `substr` on strings?
How are numbers represented in JavaScript, and when do you need `BigInt`?
How do you reliably check the type of a value in JavaScript?
If strings are primitives, how can you call methods like `"abc".toUpperCase()`?
What is the difference between `===` and `Object.is()`?

sections.title: Variables, Scope & Hoisting
sections.description: var, let and const, the three kinds of scope, hoisting and the temporal dead zone, and how execution contexts tie it all together.

questions.question: What is the difference between `var`, `let` and `const`?
What is hoisting in JavaScript? How does it differ for `var`, `let`/`const`, function declarations and function expressions?
Can you modify an object or array declared with `const`?
What are global, function and block scope in JavaScript?
What is the Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ)?
What is lexical scope and the scope chain?
Why do global `var` declarations become properties of `window` while `let` and `const` do not?
What is an execution context, and what happens in its creation and execution phases?

sections.title: Operators & Type Coercion
sections.description: == vs ===, how implicit coercion really works, the logical and nullish operators, optional chaining, spread/rest and destructuring.

questions.question: What is the difference between `==` and `===`?
What is the difference between the spread and rest operators?
How do `&&`, `||` and `??` work, and what is the difference between `||` and `??`?
What is optional chaining (`?.`)?
How does destructuring work for arrays and objects (defaults, renaming, nesting)?
How does `switch` compare values, and what is fall-through?
Explain implicit type coercion: why is `"5" + 3` `"53"` but `"5" - 3` `2`? What about `[] + {}`?
What is the difference between `Number()`, `parseInt()`, `parseFloat()` and unary `+`?
What do the logical assignment operators `||=`, `&&=` and `??=` do?
How does JavaScript convert an object to a primitive (`valueOf`, `toString`, `Symbol.toPrimitive`)?
Why is `"10" < "9"` true, and why is `null >= 0` true while `null == 0` is false?

sections.title: Functions
sections.description: Declarations vs expressions, arrow functions vs regular functions, parameters, callbacks and higher-order functions, IIFEs and pure functions.

questions.question: What are the differences between arrow functions and regular functions?
What is the difference between a function declaration and a function expression?
What are first-class functions, callbacks and higher-order functions?
How do default parameters work in JavaScript?
What is an IIFE, and why was it used?
What is a pure function, and why does it matter?
What is the `arguments` object, and why are rest parameters preferred?
What is function composition? Implement `compose` and `pipe`.
Functions are objects in JavaScript — what properties do they have, and what does that enable?

sections.title: Closures & this
sections.description: Closures and their real uses, the classic loop bug, every rule for `this`, call/apply/bind, currying and memoization.

questions.question: What is a closure in JavaScript?
What are practical use cases for closures? Show privacy, a factory and `once`.
How is `this` determined in JavaScript? Explain every context.
What is the difference between `call`, `apply` and `bind`?
What is currying? Write a generic `curry` function.
What is memoization? Implement a `memoize` function.
Can closures cause memory leaks? How?

sections.title: Objects & Arrays
sections.description: Creating and copying objects, the array methods every interview uses, mutating vs non-mutating operations, Map/Set, and JSON gotchas.

questions.question: Explain `map`, `filter`, `reduce`, `forEach`, `find`, `some`, `every` and `includes`.
What is the difference between a shallow and a deep copy? Compare spread, `Object.assign`, `JSON` and `structuredClone`.
What is the difference between `map` and `forEach`?
What is the difference between `slice` and `splice`?
What is the difference between `for...in` and `for...of`?
What are the different ways to create an object in JavaScript?
What do `Object.keys`, `Object.values` and `Object.entries` return?
How do you remove duplicates from an array and flatten a nested array?
What is the difference between `new Array(3)`, `Array.of(3)` and `Array.from()`?
What happens when you change an array’s `length` property directly?
Which array methods mutate the array, and what are their non-mutating alternatives (`toSorted`, `toReversed`…)?
Why does `[10, 9, 1].sort()` return `[1, 10, 9]`? How do you sort numbers and objects correctly?
What is the difference between `Object.freeze`, `Object.seal` and `Object.preventExtensions`?
When should you use a `Map` instead of a plain object? What about `Set`, `WeakMap` and `WeakSet`?
What are the gotchas of `JSON.stringify` and `JSON.parse`?
How does `reduce` work? Use it to count, group and index data.
How do `Map` and `Set` decide whether two keys are the same?
In what order are object properties iterated?
What are sparse arrays (holes), and how do array methods treat them?

sections.title: Prototypes & OOP
sections.description: Prototypal inheritance and the prototype chain, `__proto__` vs `prototype`, what `new` does, and ES6 classes with their modern features.

questions.question: Are ES6 classes "real" classes? What are they underneath?
What is a prototype, and how does prototypal inheritance work?
Walk through the prototype chain of an array and of a class instance.
What is the difference between `__proto__` and `prototype`?
What does the `new` keyword do, step by step?
Explain class features: `extends`, `super`, `static`, `#private` fields, getters and setters.
How does `instanceof` work?
How do you set up inheritance without classes (constructor functions and `Object.create`)?
What is the difference between a class method and an arrow-function class field?

sections.title: Asynchronous JavaScript
sections.description: The event loop, microtasks vs macrotasks, callbacks, promises and their combinators, async/await, error handling, and output-order puzzles.

questions.question: What is the event loop? Explain the call stack, Web APIs and the task queue.
What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code in JavaScript?
What is callback hell, and how do promises and async/await fix it?
What is a Promise, and what are its states?
What is the difference between microtasks and macrotasks?
What is the difference between `Promise.all`, `Promise.allSettled`, `Promise.race` and `Promise.any`?
How does promise chaining work, and how do errors propagate through a chain?
How do `async` and `await` work?
How do you handle errors with async/await?
How do you run async operations sequentially vs in parallel with `await`?
How do you convert a callback-based API into a promise-based one?
Is the function passed to `new Promise()` run synchronously or asynchronously? What happens if it throws?
How is `await` scheduled? Why can `return await` and an extra `.then` change output order?
What is an unhandled promise rejection, and how do you deal with it?
How do you add a timeout to an async operation or cancel it?

sections.title: Other Important Topics
sections.description: Debounce and throttle, timers, event propagation and delegation, modules, browser storage, strict mode and errors.

questions.question: What is the difference between `setTimeout` and `setInterval`?
What is the difference between named and default exports in ES modules?
What is the difference between `localStorage`, `sessionStorage` and cookies?
What is strict mode, and what does it change?
How do you break out of nested loops, and can you break out of `forEach`?
What is the difference between debounce and throttle? Implement both.
Explain event bubbling, capturing and event delegation.
What is the difference between CommonJS and ES modules?
What are the built-in error types, and how do you create a custom error class?
What happens when `try`, `catch` and `finally` all contain `return` statements?
What is dynamic `import()`, and when is it useful?

sections.title: Output Prediction
sections.description: Classic "what does this print?" puzzles on hoisting, the TDZ, closures, `this`, coercion and the event loop. Predict first, then reveal.

exercises.title: Check if two strings are anagrams
Flatten a nested array (recursive and iterative)

quickConcepts.question: What are the iterable and iterator protocols?
How does garbage collection work in JavaScript?
